children: Bank of Baroda’s wholly owned subsidiary, bob Securities & Giltedge Limited, has commenced operations as a non-banking financial company (NBFC-ND-ICC), with a focus on government securities and debt capital markets, the public sector lender said on October 26.

The subsidiary is expected to undertake market-making and related activities aimed at improving market efficiency and encouraging wider investor participation, including through the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Retail Direct platform, according to the bank.

Market-making involves facilitating the buying and selling of financial instruments, helping support liquidity in the market. The RBI Retail Direct platform enables individual investors to invest directly in government securities.

Debadatta Chand, Managing Director and CEO, Bank of Baroda, said the commencement of NBFC operations would lay the foundation for strengthening the bank’s presence in government securities and debt capital markets.
The launch is part of the bank’s strategy to build specialised capabilities, expand its businesses and diversify its financial services operations through dedicated subsidiaries, Chand said.
To mark the commencement of operations, bob Securities & Giltedge unveiled its corporate identity and logo and launched its website, bobgiltedge.in.
The launch event was attended by directors of Bank of Baroda and bob Securities & Giltedge, along with other dignitaries.
Bank of Baroda is majority-owned by the Government of India, which holds a 63.97% stake.

title: Bank of Baroda subsidiary commences NBFC operations, to focus on debt markets
